## [Full Frame Is 24x36mm Because a Leitz Engineer Doubled a Movie Frame in 1913](https://fstoppers.com/gear/full-frame-24x36mm-because-leitz-engineer-doubled-movie-frame-1913-904008?utm_source=fstoppers&utm_medium=RSS&utm_campaign=rss_feed_articles)
*Fstoppers* | 23/09/2026 | Score: 0.90
Tags: photography, camera, lens

> The short side of a full frame sensor is a silent-movie measurement. Cinema's full aperture ran about 24.89mm across the strip, from one row of perforations to the other, and when Oskar Barnack turned that film on its side in a workshop at Ernst Leitz in Wetzlar, that number became the height of a still photograph. The 36mm long side is two movie frames laid end to end with a millimeter or so shaved off. [ Read More ]
